title: Kannappa the Hunter
hook: a hunter brings Shiva water carried in his mouth and meat he has tasted first
carry: the heart is the real offering

segments.voice: Yesterday, Sambandar, fed by the Goddess before he asked: grace comes first, and he sang of the thief who stole his heart.

Water, carried up a hill in a man's mouth, because he has no pot. Wildflowers tucked into his hair, because his hands are full. A piece of roasted meat, which he has bitten into first, to make sure it's tender and good. A young hunter climbs into a forest shrine and lays all this before Shiva. He spits the water over the stone to wash it, shakes the flowers from his hair, sets down the meat, and stands guard all night with his bow. Today, the hunter the Tamil Shaiva saints call Kannappa.
screen: `WATER CARRIED IN HIS MOUTH.` → `FLOWERS IN HIS HAIR.` → `MEAT HE TASTED FIRST.`

segments.voice: The Periya Puranam tells it, in paraphrase. The shrine already has a priest, a careful man who comes each morning with pure water and proper flowers. Each morning he finds the place littered with bones and wilted blossoms, grieves, cleans it all, and worships again. At last Shiva tells him: hide tomorrow, and watch. The hunter arrives and sees blood running from one eye of Shiva's image. Herbs don't stop it. So he takes an arrow, cuts out his own eye, and presses it to the place. The bleeding stops, and he laughs with joy. Then the other eye of the image begins to bleed. He sets his foot on it to mark the spot, and raises the arrow again. And Shiva's hand comes out of the stone and holds his hand. Stop, Kannappa. The story doesn't mock the priest. His worship was right. But Shiva lets him see a love that knew none of the rules and held nothing back. That's bhakti at its rawest: what God receives is the heart inside the offering. Krishna says it in the Gita too, in paraphrase: a leaf, a flower, a fruit, some water, offered with love, I accept. And Sundarar, in a hymn listing the Lord's servants, names the hunter among them. One thing, plainly: this is a story about love, not a model to copy, and Shiva himself stops the hand. If you ever feel pulled to hurt yourself, call or text 988 in the US, or your local emergency number.
screen: `A PRIEST WHO GRIEVES EACH MORNING` · `THE IMAGE BEGINS TO BLEED` · `STOP, KANNAPPA` · `THE HEART IS THE OFFERING`
`IF YOU'RE HURTING: CALL OR TEXT 988 (US), OR YOUR LOCAL EMERGENCY NUMBER.`

segments.voice: If you keep a shrine or a puja shelf, offer one thing today just as it comes: a flower from outside, a glass of water, a little of your meal before you eat it, the way many Hindu families do. Don't polish it first. If you don't pray, give someone you love what's really in your hands, a tired hour, a short call, a clumsy thank-you, and let that be enough.
Tamil Shaivism and the Tevaram: Kannappa, the hunter who gave his eye to stop Shiva's image bleeding, and was stopped by Shiva's own hand. Today's word.

segments.voice: Your line: the heart is the real offering. Water from a mouth, and a hand from the stone. Rest well.

howItsDone: Kannappa is honored among the Nayanmars, the Shaiva saints of the Tamil country, and his story is told at the Shiva temple of Kalahasti, the hill shrine where tradition places it.
